worked_solution:
We find ${f}^{′}(t)$ by differentiating each component:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3}+5{t}^{2}) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{tan}⁡t) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({6}^{t})\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3{t}^{2}+10t \\ {sec}^{2}⁡t \\ {6}^{t}\operatorname{ln}⁡6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Question 10
?

Calculate f′(t) given that f(t)=[t3+5t2tan⁡t6t].

a
[3t2+10tsec2⁡t6t]
b
[3t2+10tcsc2⁡t6tln⁡6]
c
[t2+5tsec2⁡t6tln⁡6]
d
[3t2+10tsec2⁡t6tln⁡6]
e
[3t2+10tsec⁡t6tln⁡6]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We find f′(t) by differentiating each component:

f′(t)=[ddt(t3+5t2)ddt(tan⁡t)ddt(6t)]=[3t2+10tsec2⁡t6tln⁡6]
